note: Set B binds values to identifiable details and members (duct opening dimensions in DUCT FRAMING DETAIL 3, PL 4 1/2X4 1/2X1/2 with FLOOR FRAMING DETAIL C1, W10X15, L4X4X5/16) and reads the revision block correctly, whereas Set A leaves most values attached to unnamed 'structural element', 'component' or bare 'dimension' entities. Set A also invents a duct framing height of 6' (no 6' appears anywhere on the page) and repeats several facts (6 7/8", 1'-4", 1/4" TYP, the 1 1/2"=1'-0" scale) under two or three names. Set B's weaknesses are a few speculative bindings ('Detail B' for the 6" and 6 7/8" dimensions, 'Detail A' for the weld size) and a duplicated 6" claim, but it is the more faithful and informative set overall.
remarks: The text layer is in scrambled reading order, so dimension-to-detail assignment can only be resolved from the image; several of both sets' bindings (e.g. 8", 5 1/8", 2", 10") are therefore hard to verify. Both sets treat the circled '4' as a grid line ('located at grid 4' / 'grid line 4'); in the image these circled numbers and A/B bubbles are detail and section callouts, not grid lines. Set A omits W10X15, L4X4X5/16, PL 4 1/2X4 1/2X1/2, HSS 4X4X1/4, 5 7/8" and 1'-3"; Set B omits the 1 1/2" = 1'-0" drawing scales, W8X10, PL5X3/8, 2'-4 1/2", 5 1/8", 8" and 2".
